metadata.dataset_description: The dataset consists of 500 entries simulating ServiceNow fm_expense_line table, which records various attributes of financial expenses. Key fields include 'number', 'opened_at', 'amount', 'state', 'short_description', 'ci', 'user', 'department', 'category', 'process_date', 'source_id', and 'type'. This table documents the flow of financial transactions by detailing the amount, departmental allocation, and the nature of each expense. Provides a clear view of organizational expenditures across different categories, highlighting both the timing and the approval state of each financial entry.
metadata.goal: To uncover and address the reasons behind the varying rates of expense rejections across departments to improve overall financial management within the organization.

predicted_insights: IT’s rejection rate (44.19%) is about 7–9 times higher than Sales (4.92%) and Customer Support (5.99%) and, although IT submits only 8.6% of all expenses (43/500), it accounts for 41.3% of all declines (19/46), highlighting a concentrated issue in IT’s expense process.

IT exhibits consistently elevated rejection rates across all categories (Assets 0.565, Miscellaneous 0.333, Services 0.286, Travel 0.300), whereas Product Management records 0.0 in every category and HR stands out for a high Travel rejection rate (0.500), indicating department- and category-specific approval rigor.

IT’s top user rejection rate (53.85%) is over 2× Sales’ (33.33%) and 3–6× other departments’ leaders, while Product Management’s top user had 0 rejections across 12 submissions—highlighting stark department-level disparities that suggest the greatest process or policy improvement opportunity lies in IT (and secondarily Sales).

In 5 of 7 departments, expenses at/below the median are rejected more often than above-median ones (e.g., IT 50.00% vs 38.10%, HR 28.57% vs 0.00%), while Finance is the exception with stricter rejection on higher amounts (18.18% vs 0.00%), and Product Management shows no rejections in either tier—indicating department-specific controls where smaller claims often face more scrutiny except in Finance.

Assets emerges as the most frequently top-rejected category (in 3 of 7 departments), with IT’s Assets showing an exceptionally high 65% rejection rate (13 of 20), suggesting asset-related spend—especially in IT—may be a prime target for policy clarification or pre-approval controls.

IT shows persistently elevated and volatile rejection rates—including two months at 100% (2024-02 and 2024-03) and several at 50–60%—while Finance has sharp spikes to 50% in 2024-02 and 2024-04 despite many 0% months; by contrast, Customer Support stays low (0–21.43%, mostly under 14%), Sales peaks at 25% in 2024-03, HR has a one-off 66.67% in 2023-11, and Product Management is consistently 0% when present—indicating that root-cause analysis should prioritize IT (systemic issues) and Finance (episodic spikes).

The median processed expense varies markedly across departments—from 3045 (HR) to 5832 (Product Management), a 91.6% difference—implying materially different spending baselines that may merit department-specific controls, while the absence of completed declines suggests most rejections likely occur before completion (e.g., during Pending/Submitted stages).

IT’s rejection rates are both the highest and most volatile—peaking for mid-range amounts at 66.7% in Q2—while Finance rejects only mid-range expenses (25.0% in Q3) and Product Management has zero rejections in every quartile; meanwhile, Customer Support and Sales generally show lower and decreasing decline rates as amounts increase.

Above 2,577, IT accounts for 54% of all declines (13 of 24) despite only 9.5% of submissions (24 of 253), with an aggregate high-amount rejection rate of 54% versus 3.9% in Customer Support and 4.6% in Sales—pointing to department-specific policy or review intensity as the key driver rather than amount alone.

Only 2 of 7 departments (HR and Customer Support) see higher rejection with missing source_id, with HR showing a large +41.67 pp gap, while 4 departments (including IT at −19.23 pp and Finance at −13.33 pp) actually have higher rejection when source_id is populated—indicating department-specific processes drive rejections more than the mere presence of source_id.

High-amount expenses are not uniformly more likely to be rejected—only IT (+16.67 pp: 66.67% vs 50.00%) and Finance (+13.89 pp: 25.00% vs 11.11%) show higher top-quartile rejection, while Customer Support, Sales, Development, and HR show lower rejection for high-amounts by 2.84–25.00 pp, with Product Management at 0% across both groups (noting small top-quartile sample sizes in several departments).

Processed decision times vary widely across departments (median ≈94 hours overall, ranging from 33.96 hours in IT to 191.57 hours in Product Management—about a 5.6x spread), and the lack of computable Declined medians suggests either very few declines or missing processing timestamps, both of which warrant review to understand rejection patterns.
predicted_summary:
IT is the clear outlier in expense rejections: it has the highest overall rate at 44.19% (19/43), stays elevated every month among completed expenses (often around 50% and peaking at 100% in Feb–Mar 2024), and rejects across all amount ranges (quartiles: 38.5%–66.7%). Within IT, the Assets category is the main hotspot (65.0% rejected, 13/20), and individual contributors show high rates (e.g., 53.85% for the top submitter with ≥5 entries).
Rejection likelihood depends on expense size in different ways by department: smaller expenses tend to be rejected more in Customer Support (8.96% at/below median vs 3.01% above) and Sales (6.56% vs 3.28%), and especially in HR (28.57% vs 0.00%), with quartiles echoing this (e.g., Customer Support 10.6% in the lowest quartile vs 4.8% in the highest; Sales 9.1% vs 2.9%). Finance shows the opposite pattern—larger expenses are more often rejected (18.18% above median vs 0.00% below; top quartile 25.0% vs 11.11% for the rest)—while IT remains high regardless of amount (e.g., top quartile 66.67% vs 50.00% for the bottom three quartiles).
Process and category signals align with higher rejections and vary by department: missing source_id is strongly associated with more rejections in HR (+41.67 percentage points, 50.00% vs 8.33%), but the reverse pattern appears in IT (−19.23 pp, 30.77% vs 50.00%). The highest-rejection categories differ by team—IT: Assets 65.0% (13/20); Finance: Assets 22.2% (2/9); Sales: Miscellaneous 25.0% (1/4); Customer Support: Miscellaneous 16.7% (1/6)—and within-department submitters show sizable variation (e.g., Sales 33.33% for the top frequent submitter; Customer Support 22.22%), indicating that documentation and category mix are key drivers of the observed differences.
